items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I use Louis Armstrong’s philosophy. You convert fans into friends.

ctx.x: So these people helped make you famous again.

Short changed, man. You know, I’ve just been fortunate, man. I’ve been blessed, that’s what I’ve been. I’ve been blessed, man, because, you know, I’ve only had a publicist once. That didn’t last too long but anyway, I don’t have -- maybe I should be getting one now because -­ But the philosophy -- I use Louis Armstrong’s philosophy. You convert fans into friends. Fans are fickle but you become friends, man, they’ll support you period. Because after Pops chops were gone, everything -- people still came out to see…

Well let’s go back to your appearance -- you know, they documented it on Jazz On A Summer’s Day up in Newport and you have Eric Dolphy on there. I know you mentioned that you started with Buddy, but when Buddy turned left on you brought Jerome Richardson out.
